title: Deterministic Upgrade Oracle and Artifact Provenance Spec for Sealed/VPC Deploys
creator: Aisha Patel
description: This PRD defines a reproducible, deterministic upgrade validation harness (the 'Upgrade Oracle') and a mandatory artifact provenance verification flow for Private/VPC deployments. The goal is to ensure upgrades can be simulated and validated in air-gapped or minimal-egress environments before operator rollout, and that artifact provenance (signatures, SBOM, transitive dependency attestations) is verifiable without internet egress.
problem_statement: Customers operating in sealed or highly restricted networks lack a deterministic, repeatable way to validate that a candidate runtime/operator image and associated artifacts will behave identically post-upgrade across their nodes. Existing acceptance criteria rely on ad-hoc operator checks and manual artifact ingestion which produces variability and increases rollback risk.
rationale: Providing a deterministic validation harness reduces upgrade regressions, shortens troubleshooting windows, and is a strong compliance signal for customers in regulated environments. Combined with cryptographic provenance checks, it raises the bar for supply-chain integrity for offline upgrades.
goals: Define a deterministic execution oracle that can replay a bounded upgrade scenario and generate stable evidence (checksums, traces, runtime invariants) across 3+ replica nodes
Mandate artifact provenance verification steps that are executable in air-gapped environments (signed manifests, SBOM, and notary/attestation verification using customer KMS or offline signing keys)
Produce an operator-facing acceptance matrix and automated harness tools that can run inside customer networks (operatorless execution optional)
Integrate telemetry contracts so that any deviation from the oracle's expected outputs surfaces actionable errors in the Console and runbook
non_goals: Provide a one-click fully-automated upgrade for every custom topology (we will provide a deterministic test harness and operator playbooks but not end-to-end automation for every bespoke setup)
Replace customer change management policies; this is an evidence-producing validation tool, not a decision engine
Ship new cryptographic hardware (HSM) — we will integrate with existing KMS/HSM providers via documented procedures
constraints: Must run without outbound internet connectivity (air-gapped) using mirror repositories or pre-staged artifacts
Evidence artifacts (checksum bundles, traces) must be size-bounded for offline transfer and human review
Acceptance checks must complete within a configurable timeout (default 90 minutes) for typical small clusters (3-5 nodes)
Tooling must respect customer RBAC and not necessitate cluster admin credentials beyond standard operator privileges
acceptance_criteria: Oracle run: Ability to perform a simulated upgrade on a 3-node cluster that produces a deterministic 'evidence bundle' (signed JSON and checksums) that matches across nodes when run with the same input seed

Artifact provenance: Candidate runtime/operator images and all transitive artifacts must have a signed manifest and a verifiable SBOM; the verification flow must be executable offline using customer-provided public keys or root-of-trust bundles

Mismatch handling: If checksums, SBOM hashes, or runtime invariants differ across nodes, the harness must fail with documented error classes and produce a triage artifact linking to the Console runbook
Operator gate: The upgrade plan must expose a human-approved gate that requires review of the evidence bundle before allowing a live rollout to proceed

Airgap compatibility: All necessary verification tooling, scripts, and dependency archives must be runnable from a local mirror or pre-seeded artifact bundle; no external calls to public registries during validation

Telemetry contract: Validation runs must emit signed telemetry entries (or local telemetry files for air-gapped sites) that include start/finish timestamps, outcome codes, and compact invariant diffs; Console ingestion and dashboarding for non-airgapped customers must show these results
Reproducibility: Re-running the oracle with identical inputs must yield identical evidence bundle checksums across at least three independent runs
Documentation: Operator playbook, runbook, and offline artifact preparation checklist published in Confluence with step-by-step commands and example expected outputs
upgrade_validation_steps: 1) Prepare mirror: Operator creates a local mirror of required container archives and operator images and a signed manifest (example script provided)
2) Seed harness: Upload or place harness binary, seed configuration, and signed manifest into the cluster control plane or operator namespace
3) Run simulation: Execute the deterministic upgrade oracle with a seeded traffic emulator and KV cache warm-up sequence; collect runtime invariants and traces
4) Collect evidence: Harness signs and bundles checksums, SBOM hashes, and a short trace snapshot into an evidence bundle
5) Verify provenance: Run offline signature verification against customer root-of-trust and validate SBOM contents match manifest
6) Gate decision: Present bundle to operator via CLI/UI; operator approves to continue or aborts and files a rollback ticket
7) Post-check: After approval, run a short smoke validation (latency p95, token correctness for a few prompts) before promoting to full rollout
telemetry_requirements: For online customers: events pushed to Console with types: validation.start, validation.succeed, validation.fail, provenance.mismatch; include run_id and bundle checksum
For air-gapped customers: produce signed local telemetry files and an exportable audit archive; include minimal PII and operator identity hash
Telemetry must include duration, number of nodes validated, list of artifacts verified, and a short invariant diff summary
Failure events must contain a prioritized triage key that maps to runbook sections and suggested mitigations
test_matrix: Small cluster (3 nodes) with standard operator, mirror size < 10GB, run full oracle — expected: pass within 60 mins
Medium cluster (5-10 nodes) partial mirror with spotty node load — expected: pass within 90 mins or produce deterministic mismatch report
Hardware variance test: same image but different CPU/GPU family; oracle should surface kernel selection or quantization mismatch as a non-fatal warning unless functional invariants fail
Offline provenance negative test: corrupt one artifact signature in the manifest — expected: harness fails with provenance.mismatch and returns explicit signed-bundle diff
KV cache compatibility test: upgrade that changes cache layout — expected: harness detects cache invalidation and logs deterministic divergence with mitigation suggestions
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (canary in staging): Run harness in Redwood staging closed-network; document timings and false-positive rates
Phase 1 (customer pilot): Select 2 customers (one air-gapped, one minimal-egress) to run the harness with support from Solutions Eng
Phase 2 (general availability): Bundle CLI + operator charts + Confluence runbook; require security sign-off and ship in private-2026.04
Rollback policy: If evidence bundle indicates mismatches, automate cluster-level rollback to previous operator image; require postmortem before reattempt
success_metrics: Reduction in upgrade-induced incidents for Private customers by 50% within 3 months of GA
Mean time to detect upgrade regressions reduced from operator-reported 4 hours to harness-detected < 30 minutes
At least 90% reproducibility rate for oracle runs in pilot customers (identical evidence bundle checksums across 3 runs)
Adoption: 30% of new private deployments use the harness in their first upgrade within 6 months
risks_mitigations: Risk: False positives due to non-deterministic workload seeds — Mitigation: provide deterministic seed fixtures and a seed validation tool
Risk: Customers unwilling to pre-mirror large artifact sets — Mitigation: provide compressed delta bundles and clear sizing guidance
Risk: Signature/key distribution complexity for offline sites — Mitigation: document an offline root-of-trust bootstrap procedure and provide support-run checklist
Risk: Over-reliance on harness masking real operator issues — Mitigation: require manual operator gate and maintain runbook remediation steps
dependencies: ENG-40312: Operator chart: readable evidence-bundle API
ENG-41877: CLI verifier and offline signature tooling
ENG-42901: Console telemetry ingestion endpoints and dashboard widgets
PM-712001: Pilot customer selection and pilot support schedule
notes: Coordinate with Security for offline key transfer SOP and for SBOM minimal disclosure policy
